text: Commit signatures as user identities in git
description:
Felix 2026-11-11: represent users by commit signatures, staying on git and signing with different user identities. "Something we might want to implement regardless of how we implement the host version."

Why: a commit's author and its Co-Authored-By line are free text, so anyone can commit as anyone. The last 300 commits here are unsigned and all authored by Felix; agents appear only as a text trailer.

How it can work: each person and each agent has a key (git signs commits with SSH keys); a list of names and public keys lives in the repo, so every clone can verify who signed which commit; the key is chosen per commit, so several identities can sign on one machine.

status.comment: Wanted by Felix, not designed. To settle: where the list of keys lives and who may add a key to it, how agents get their keys, and whether the shared branch requires signed commits.
